title: Trust and civic action diverge across joint gig-work and student-debt conditions

observations.period: 2024; no gig work and no student-loan responsibility
observations.method: Weighted CCES common-post respondent comparison using commonpostweight; federal/state trust coded positive as a great deal or fair amount and civic action as at least one positive response across six selected action fields.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive weighted comparison without complex-survey variance in this pass; post-election cross-section lacks event timing, attribution, prior trust history, and causal identification.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting neither gig work nor current student-loan responsibility.
observations.counterinterpretation: Joint outcomes reflect income, age, education, race, party identity, employment, selection, and question-universe differences; proxies are not dated material shocks.

observations.method: Weighted CCES common-post respondent comparison using commonpostweight; federal/state trust coded positive as a great deal or fair amount and civic action as at least one positive response across six selected action fields.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive weighted comparison without complex-survey variance in this pass; the smallest proxy cell has 665 respondents and cross-sectional material proxies do not establish a dated pathway.
observations.subgroup: Respondents reporting both gig work and current student-loan responsibility.
observations.counterinterpretation: The joint high-trust/action share may reflect age, education, political identity, work selection, or other composition rather than a material condition causing civic action.

related_sources.claim: Prior CCES subgroup layer conditions separate trust and action measures on income and race.

boundary: This record measures joint co-occurrence of trust and civic action within four material/work proxy cells. It does not establish that gig work or student debt caused trust, action, vote, or political meaning, and it has no complex-design variance estimate.
